prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

This automatic driving assistance device automatically performs least a part of vehicle control including steering, braking, and acceleration and deceleration within a predetermined travel section. The automatic driving assistance device includes: a switching section determination unit that determines, in the travel section, a section in which a first load that is based on a road shape or a road structure becomes equal to or less than a predetermined threshold as a switching section in which the at least a part of the vehicle control is switched from automatic driving to manual driving; a driving action planning unit that, when the vehicle enters the determined switching section, generates an automatic driving action plan so that a second load that is based on a travel situation of nearby vehicles around the vehicle is reduced; and a driving switching unit that ends automatic driving that is based on the automatic driving action plan and switches the automatic driving to the manual driving.

outputs.L4:
An automatic driving assistance device is configured to support a safe and smooth transition from automated driving to manual driving. During automated operation, the device controls vehicle functions such as steering, braking, and acceleration while continuously monitoring the planned route, road geometry, traffic conditions, and the behavior of nearby vehicles.

When a transition to manual driving is required, the device searches the route ahead for a road section in which the driver’s expected workload is relatively low. Such a section may include, for example, a straight road with good visibility, moderate vehicle speed, few intersections or lane changes, and limited surrounding traffic. Sections involving sharp curves, congestion, merging traffic, construction, or other complex conditions may be excluded because they would place a greater burden on the driver immediately after the handover.

After identifying a suitable transition section, the device plans and performs vehicle actions intended to create favorable conditions for transferring control. These actions may include adjusting the vehicle’s speed, increasing the distance from a preceding vehicle, avoiding travel alongside another vehicle, selecting an appropriate lane, or timing the handover so that nearby traffic presents less risk. The device may also provide advance visual, audible, or tactile notifications to prompt the driver to prepare to resume control.

Once the vehicle reaches the selected low-load section and the required safety conditions are satisfied, the system requests that the driver take control. The automated driving function is ended after the driver’s readiness or control input is confirmed. By selecting an appropriate location and reducing the influence of surrounding traffic before the transition, the device enables automated driving to be terminated under safer and less demanding road and traffic conditions, thereby reducing driver workload and improving the reliability of the handover.

**“This” and “The”**

“This” and “the” are common English determiners, but they serve different purposes. **“This”** identifies a specific person, object, or idea that is close to the speaker or currently being discussed: *“This book is fascinating.”* It can also stand alone as a pronoun: *“This is my favorite.”*

**“The”** is the definite article. It refers to someone or something already known, previously mentioned, or unique: *“The book on the table is mine.”* While “this” draws attention to a particular item, “the” simply shows that its identity is clear from the context.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an automatic driving assistance device that selects a low-road-complexity section for handover to manual driving and reduces traffic-related load before switching control to the driver.
counterfactuals.output: An automatic driving assistance device includes a road-information acquisition unit configured to acquire information indicating road complexity along a planned travel route, a section-selection unit configured to select a handover section having road complexity lower than a predetermined threshold, and a traffic-load reduction unit configured to reduce a traffic-related load on a vehicle before the vehicle reaches the selected handover section. The traffic-related load may be reduced by controlling vehicle speed, adjusting an inter-vehicle distance, changing a travel lane, or selecting a handover timing based on surrounding-vehicle conditions. A handover control unit issues a request for a driver to assume a manual driving operation and switches control of the vehicle from automatic driving to manual driving within the selected handover section after the traffic-related load has been reduced. Accordingly, the device enables transfer of driving authority in a road environment and traffic condition that facilitate driver recognition and operation, thereby improving the safety and smoothness of the handover.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an autonomous vehicle control system with three components: a switching-section determination unit, a driving-action planning unit, and a driving-switching unit.
counterfactuals.output:
An autonomous vehicle control system may include the following three components:

1. **Switching-Section Determination Unit**  
   Identifies sections of a planned route in which the vehicle should change its driving mode or control strategy. Using map data, vehicle position, traffic conditions, road geometry, sensor reliability, and system capabilities, it may designate boundaries between autonomous-driving sections, manual-driving sections, or sections requiring a different level of automation.

2. **Driving-Action Planning Unit**  
   Generates a driving plan for each section. The plan may specify lane keeping, lane changes, acceleration, braking, turning, stopping, obstacle avoidance, and target speed. For an approaching switching section, the unit also plans preparatory actions, such as reducing speed, moving to a suitable lane, increasing following distance, or requesting that the driver take control.

3. **Driving-Switching Unit**  
   Performs the actual transition at or near the determined switching section. It changes control between autonomous and driver-operated modes, or between different autonomous-control strategies, based on the planned actions and current safety conditions. The unit may issue advance notifications, verify driver readiness, transfer steering and pedal authority gradually, and delay or cancel a transition if the required conditions are not satisfied.

Together, the components determine **where** a control transition should occur, plan **how** the vehicle should approach and pass through that transition, and execute the switch **safely and smoothly**.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain, using formal technical language, how an automated driving assistance system can choose a manual-driving transition section based on road-related load and reduce the load caused by surrounding traffic before completing the transition.
counterfactuals.output:
An automated driving assistance system may determine a suitable manual-driving transition section by separately evaluating **road-related driving load** and **surrounding-traffic-related driving load**.

1. **Candidate-section identification**  
   Using map data, route information, localization results, and forward sensing, the system identifies candidate sections in which control may be transferred from automated driving to the human driver.

2. **Road-related load estimation**  
   For each candidate section, the system computes a road-load index representing the intrinsic difficulty of manual operation. Relevant parameters may include:
   - road curvature and curvature variation;
   - gradient and lane width;
   - number of lanes, merges, diverges, and intersections;
   - visibility, road-surface condition, and speed limit; and
   - required frequency or magnitude of steering, braking, and acceleration inputs.

   A representative formulation is
   \[
   L_{\mathrm{road}}(s)=\sum_i w_i f_i(s),
   \]
   where \(s\) denotes position, \(f_i\) are normalized road-complexity factors, and \(w_i\) are weighting coefficients. The system selects a transition section in which \(L_{\mathrm{road}}\) remains below a prescribed threshold for at least a minimum distance or time.

3. **Traffic-load estimation**  
   The system detects nearby vehicles and estimates a traffic-load index from relative distance, relative velocity, time headway, time to collision, lateral proximity, cut-in probability, and traffic density. For example,
   \[
   L_{\mathrm{traffic}}=g(h_f,h_r,\Delta v_f,\Delta v_r,\rho,p_{\mathrm{cut\text{-}in}}),
   \]
   where \(h_f\) and \(h_r\) are front and rear headways and \(\rho\) is local traffic density.

4. **Pre-transition load-reduction control**  
   Before issuing or completing the handover, the automated system modifies the host vehicle’s motion to reduce \(L_{\mathrm{traffic}}\). It may:
   - gradually decelerate or accelerate to increase front and rear time headways;
   - avoid remaining alongside another vehicle;
   - change lanes to a lane having lower traffic density or fewer merging conflicts;
   - complete an ongoing overtake, merge, or lane change under automated control; or
   - shift the handover point within the selected road section until surrounding-traffic conditions are acceptable.

   These maneuvers are subject to safety, comfort, legality, and vehicle-dynamics constraints.

5. **Transition completion**  
   The system requests manual takeover only when both the road-load criterion and the traffic-load criterion are satisfied:
   \[
   L_{\mathrm{road}}\leq T_{\mathrm{road}},\qquad
   L_{\mathrm{traffic}}\leq T_{\mathrm{traffic}}.
   \]
   During a confirmation interval, the system verifies driver readiness, such as visual attention and contact with the controls. Automated control is maintained until the driver acknowledges the request and stable manual control is detected. If the traffic load cannot be sufficiently reduced within the selected section, the system postpones the transition, selects a later section, or executes a minimum-risk maneuver.

Thus, the transition location is selected primarily according to the inherent complexity of the road, while active longitudinal and lateral control is used before handover to create a lower-load surrounding-traffic state.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent specification passage for an automatic-to-manual vehicle control handover system that uses a first threshold-based load associated with road geometry and a second load associated with the travel conditions of nearby vehicles.
counterfactuals.output:
In an embodiment, a vehicle control system is configured to selectively transition a vehicle from an automated driving mode to a manual driving mode. The system includes one or more processors configured to receive road-geometry data representing at least a curvature, gradient, lane width, intersection configuration, merge region, or visibility characteristic of a road segment ahead of the vehicle. The processors determine a first control load based on the road-geometry data and compare the first control load with a first threshold. The processors further receive travel-condition data for one or more nearby vehicles, the travel-condition data including at least one of relative distance, relative velocity, predicted trajectory, traffic density, lane-change activity, or time to collision. Based on the travel-condition data, the processors determine a second control load representing an interaction load attributable to the nearby vehicles and compare the second control load with a second threshold.

When the first control load satisfies the first threshold and the second control load satisfies the second threshold, the processors initiate a handover procedure from the automated driving mode to the manual driving mode. The handover procedure may include issuing an audible, visual, or haptic request for a driver to assume control, monitoring driver readiness, and maintaining automated longitudinal and lateral control during a predetermined handover interval. In some implementations, the handover procedure is initiated when a combined load, determined from a weighted or nonlinear combination of the first and second control loads, satisfies a handover criterion, even if only one of the first and second thresholds is individually satisfied. The thresholds or weighting factors may be dynamically adjusted according to vehicle speed, weather, sensor confidence, driver state, or an estimated time remaining before the vehicle reaches the road segment associated with the first control load. If driver readiness is not detected within the handover interval, the system may cause the vehicle to enter a minimum-risk condition, including reducing vehicle speed, increasing following distance, changing lanes, or stopping at a selected location.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
